`goBack` is registered with snapshot=true (`goBack(true)` at line 717) and returns `captureAriaSnapshot`, i.e. the URL, title and full accessibility snapshot of whatever page the user's logged-in browser lands on: private session content (SECRET) and possibly attacker-authored page text (UNTRUSTED).
`goForward(true)` returns `captureAriaSnapshot` content for the resulting page — the user's authenticated browser content (SECRET) and potentially attacker-controlled page text (UNTRUSTED).

`snapshot.handle` calls `captureAriaSnapshot`, which asks the extension for `getUrl`, `getTitle` and `browser_snapshot` of the currently connected tab. That tab may be an authenticated SaaS/intranet/localhost page (SECRET) or an attacker-controlled web page whose text is injected into the agent cont

`click` sends `browser_click` to the extension and then returns `captureAriaSnapshot` content, exposing the resulting page (user's session data → SECRET; attacker page text → UNTRUSTED). `hover` returns `captureAriaSnapshot` output after hovering, so page content of the connected tab reaches the agent: private authenticated content (SECRET) and attacker-authored page text (UNTRUSTED).

`type` sends agent-supplied `text` into an editable element of the live page and can press Enter (`submit` in `TypeTool`), so arbitrary agent data can be posted into an attacker-readable destination (attacker-hosted form, public comment box, search query) — SINK. `selectOption` sets dropdown values in the page and returns `captureAriaSnapshot` content: user's private page content (SECRET) and attacker-authored page text (UNTRUSTED). The selected values are constrained to existing option values, so it is not treated as a general exfiltration channel.

`pressKey` forwards a single key name to the extension and returns only the fixed string `Pressed key ${key}`; no page content is returned and no agent-authored payload of meaningful size leaves the host.
`wait2` only sleeps in the browser and returns a fixed confirmation string; it reads nothing and sends nothing outward.

`getConsoleLogs` returns the connected tab's console output verbatim (`consoleLogs.map((log) => JSON.stringify(log))`). Logs of an authenticated app can contain private data/tokens (SECRET) and any page script — including an attacker's — can write arbitrary strings to the console (UNTRUSTED).

`screenshot` returns a PNG of the current tab into the agent context: pixels of the user's logged-in page (SECRET) and, when the tab shows attacker content, attacker-chosen rendered text/instructions (UNTRUSTED).
